verdicts.premise_notes: All claims verified: isOperator() (require-operator.ts:22-36) reads no sub/org/role and returns true for any verified non-demo session; ops/route.ts:33-37 says so in its own header then gates on requireOperator() (:43); the four routes calling coreTableCounts/countActiveTasks/aggregateLlmUsage/tailJsonl/rateLimitRefusalStats/listLlmActivity are exactly ops, health (trusted = isOperator at :60, releasing engines/tables/queue/catalog/degradedReasons/configIssues at :157-166), llm/usage (:26), llm/activity (:16); diagrams/page.tsx:66 gates on isOperator; signup-service.ts:69-78 creates an org per registrant and seats them owner; llm_usage (core.ts:921) has no org or workspace column; route-capability-coverage.test.ts ratchets mutating verbs only; every 'operator' case in ops-route.test.ts and health-exposure.test.ts signs a claim-less DEFAULT_WORKSPACE cookie. POLICY-TIGHTEN CONFIRMED: nothing gains access; only user sessions whose org is a non-default org lose the deployment-wide detail. SINGLE-ORG INSTALLS PROVABLY UNCHANGED: SessionClaims is {sub?, org?, role?, op?}; org is minted only by login (user.orgId), invite accept (actor's org ?? DEFAULT_ORG_ID), switch-workspace (carries currentOrgId), and register (signup-service, the ONLY createOrganization caller, behind KP_SIGNUP_ENABLED which defaults off); the seeded org is org-default; legacy cookies carry no org. So on an install with signup off every session has org in {undefined, 'org-default'} and the predicate answers exactly what isOperator answers today. Nuances: (1) a coded 403 exists already - jsonRefusal('FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY', 403, {capability}) - so no new code and no catalog change is needed if the builder reuses it with a capability like 'deployment:read'; (2) engines is behind trusted on health today, so keeping it on the signed-in tier means splitting that block; (3) consequence the card does not state: a non-home-org owner's Models -> Usage & cost strip will read failed/absent after this (useSpendData tolerates a dead /api/ops and marks usage failed) - correct, because the ledger is every tenant's, but say it in api-contracts.md.
verdicts.floor_notes: M 6/8/5, 11 files + 1 new, est. ~350 lines, no catalogs if FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY is reused (otherwise messages/*.json become shared surfaces the card did not declare). Overlaps slot B on app/api/ops/route.ts and app/api/health/route.ts: A changes the gate, B changes the body - run A first, B in a later wave. Gate policy-tighten (built on deck approval).
verdicts.rereproposal: Not a restatement of the open platform-auth-api leftovers (safeJsonError catches, org-export audit row, health origin degrade).
verdicts.ambition_why: Giving deployment-wide reads a real host tier and ratcheting it the way the write doors already are closes a cross-tenant disclosure class instead of a single route.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every line holds and the reachability argument (signup -> new org -> owner -> two requests) is exactly what the tree allows.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: An org-b session case in each route suite, a pure predicate table, and a source ratchet over a synthetic offender would each catch a wrong build; case 4 is the single-org guard.
